Heterogeneous origin (LGE/dLGE + cortical); pick a defensible single canonical master (e.g. OTP for some hypothalamo-amygdala nuclei, or LHX6 for MGE-derived) after a short lit check before fetch. [v1.12 RESOLVED-OPEN: primary developmental-neuroscience literature confirms the amygdala is genuinely multi-origin with NO single canonical master TF — CeM/ISL1(vLGE), CeC-CeL/PAX6(dLGE), CeA/DLX5(striatal), MeA/LHX5-6-9+OTP(hypothalamic), POA-derived/DBX1+FOXP2, BLA/DBX1-EMX1(pallial). Forcing one master would over-claim. Documented as legitimately open in brain_region_master_survey.json. Sources: Front Mol Neurosci 2024(1364268), Front Neuroanat 2022(883537), eLife 2017(PMC5384829), PubMed 29869132.]

Shares NKX2-1 with pallidum/hypothalamus; confirm distinct promoter target or fold into hypothalamus. [v1.12 RESOLVED-SHARED: NKX2-1 is shared with pallidum AND hypothalamus — an independent POA atlas entry would double-count one already-locked promoter (the pallidum NKX2-1 lock). POA is additionally internally parcellated (multiple niche identities, not one master). Resolved as 'shared master, not independent organ'; correctly excluded from the single-master atlas to avoid promoter double-counting. Sources: J Neurosci 2007(9682), eLife 2017(PMC5384829).]

Confirm canonical septal master before fetch. [v1.12 RESOLVED-OPEN: the ZIC family (ZIC1-5) is expressed in the septum in an overlapping/redundant manner and is NOT septum-specific — the same ZIC pattern appears in thalamus, POA, cortical hem, and retina. No single ZIC gene is a canonical septum master; picking one would be arbitrary and non-specific. Documented as legitimately open in brain_region_master_survey.json. Sources: PMC11113920, PMC6672357(J Neurosci 2007), Dev Dyn 2007.]
